source_text: Unius igitur et ejusdem substantize sunt omnia, hoc est, ab uno et eodem Deo, quemadmodum et Dominus ait discipulis: Propterea omnis scriba doctus in regno ceclorum similis est homini patrifamilias, qui profert de thesauro suo nova et vetera. Non alterum quidem vetera, alterum vero proferentem nova docuit; sed unum et eundem. Paterfamilias enim Dominus est, qui universe domui paternee dominatur: et servis quidem et adhuce indisciplinatis condignam tradens legem; liberis autem et fide justificatis congruentia dans precepta, et filiis adaperiens suam heereditatem. Scribas autem et doctores regni ccelorum, suos dicebat discipulos, de quibus et alibi ait Judzis: Hece mitto ad sapientes, et scribas, et doctores, et ex eis occidetis, et effugabitis a civitate in civitatem. Sic itaque que de thesauro proferuntur nova et vetera, sine contradictione duo testamenta dicit: vetus quidem quod ante fuerat legisdatio ; novum autem, que secundum Evangelium est conversatio, ostendit, de qua David ait: Cantate Domino canticum novoum. Et Esaias: Cantate Domino hymmum novum. Initium ejus, glorificatur nomen ejus a summo terre: virtutes ejus in insulis annuntiant. Et Hieremias ait: Ecce disponam, inquit, ¢estamentum nooum, non quemadmodum disposui patribus vestris in monte Oreb. Utraque autem testamenta unus et idem paterfamilias produxit, Verbum Dei, Dominus noster Jesus Christus, qui et Abrahze et Moysi collocutus est, qui nobis in novitate restituit libertatem, et multiplicavit eam, quee ab ipso est, 1. Plus est enim, inquit, templo hic. Plus autem et minus non in his dicitur, quee inter se communionem non habent, et sunt contrarize naturee, et pugnant adversus se; sed in his quee ejusdem sunt substantize, et communicant secum, solum autem multitudine et magnitudine differunt : quemadmodum aqua ab aqua, et lumen a lumine, et gratia a gratia. Major est igitur legisdatio que in libertatem, quam quz data est in servitutem: et ideo non in unam gentem, sed in totum mundum diffusa est. Unus autem et idem Dominus, qui plus quam templum est, et plus quam Salomon, et plus quam Jonas donat hominibus, id est, suam preesentiam et resurrectionem a mortuis: sed non Deum immutans, nec alium spreedicans Patrem, sed eundem ipsum, qui semper habet plura domesticis, et proficiente eorum erga Deum dilectione, plura et majora donans, quemadmodum et Dominus discipulis dicebat: Quoniam et majora horum videbitis, Et Paulus ait: * Non quod jam acceperim, aut quod justificatus sim, aut jam persim: ex parte enim scimus, et ex parte prophetamus. Cum autem venerit quod perfectum est, que sunt ex parte, destruentur. Sicut igitur adveniente perfecto, non alterum Patrem videbimus, sed hune quem nune videre concupimus: Beati enim mundi corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt; neque alium Christum et Dei Filium exspectabimus, sed hune qui ex Maria * Virgine, qui et passus est, in quem et credimus, quem et diligimus; quemadmodum Esaias ait: Hé¢ dicent in illa die: Ecce, Dominus Deus noster, in quem speravimus, et exultavimus in salute nostra, Et Petrus ait in epistola sua: Quem non videntes diligitis, inquit, in quem nunc non videntes credidistis, gaudebitis gaudio inenarrabili ; neque alium Spiritum sanctum percipimus, nisi hune qui est nobiscum, et qui clamat, Absa, Pater ; et in iisdem ipsis augmentum habebimus, et proficiemus, ut jam non per speculum, et per eenigmata, sed facie ad faciem fruamur muneribus Dei: sic et nunc plus temet plus Salomone percipientes, quod est adventus Filii Dei, non alterum didicimus Deum, preter fabricatorem et factorem omnium, qui ab initio nobis demonstratus est; neque alterum Christum Dei Filium, preeter eum qui a prophetis preedicatus est. 2. Novo enim Testamento cognito et preedicato per prophetas, et ille qui illud dispositurus erat secundum placitum Patris preedicabatur, manifestatus hominibus quemadmodum voluit Deus; ut possint semper proficere credentes in eum, et per testamenta Una enim salus et unus Deus; quee autem formant hominem, preecepta multa, et non pauci qui adducunt hominem ad Deum. Terreno quidem et temporali regi, cum sit homo, licet aliquoties majores profectus attribuere his qui sunt subjecti: Deo autem non licebit, cum sit idem, et semper majorem gratiam preestare humano generi velit, et pluribus muneribus assidue honorare eos qui placent ei? hoe est proficere, alterum adinvenire Patrem preeter eum qui ab initio annuntiatus est, et rursum, preeter eum qui putatur secundo inyentus esse, alterum tertium adinvenire ; et ejusdem erit profectus et a tertio in quartum, et ab hoc rursum alterum et alterum: et sic semper putans proficere talis sensus, nunquam in stabit Deo. Expulsus enim ab eo qui est, et reversus retrorsum, quzeretquidem semper, inyeniet‘autem nunquam Deum ; sed semper incomprehensibilitatis profundo natabit, nisi per poenitentiam conversus, unde et abjectus erat, revertatur, unum Deum Patrem Demiurgum confitens et credens, qui a Lege et prophetis annuntiatus est, qui a Christo testificatus est, quemadmodum ipse ait ad eos qui accusabant ejus discipulos, quasi non servarent traditionem seniorum: Quare vos frustramini preeceptum Domini propter traditionem vestram? Deus enim dixit: Honora patrem et matrem; et, Qui maledixerit patri aut matri, morte moriatur. Et iterum secundo ait eis: Ht frustrati estis sermonem Dei propter vestram; manifestissime Patrem et Deum confitens Christus eum qui in Lege dixit: Honora patrem et matrem, ut tibi bene sit. Verbum enim Dei confessus est Legis preeceptum verax Deus, et neminem alterum Deum appellavit, quam suum Patrem.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, all things are of one and the same substance, that is, from one and the same God, just as also the Lord says to the disciples: Therefore, every scribe who is learned in the kingdom of heaven is like a householder who brings forth from his treasure new and old things. For he did not teach that one brings forth old things and another brings forth new things, but one and the same. For the Lord is the householder who rules over the whole house paternally, and to the servants, indeed, and those still undisciplined, he gives a law worthy of them, but to the children, justified by faith, he gives fitting precepts, and to the sons, he opens his inheritance. And he calls his disciples scribes and teachers of the kingdom of heaven, about whom he also says elsewhere to the Jews: Behold, I send to the wise and scribes and teachers, and you will kill and persecute them from city to city. Thus, therefore, the new and old things that are brought forth from the treasure say, without contradiction, two testaments: the old, indeed, which was the legislation before, and the new, which is the conversation according to the Gospel, which David says: Sing to the Lord a new song, and Isaiah: Sing to the Lord a new hymn. The beginning of it, his name is glorified from the top of the earth, his virtues are announced in the islands. And Jeremiah says: Behold, I will make a new testament, not as I made with your fathers in Mount Horeb. Both testaments, however, one and the same householder produced, the Word of God, our Lord Jesus Christ, who spoke with Abraham and Moses, who restored to us in newness liberty and multiplied it, which is from him. For he says: This is greater than the temple, and greater than Solomon, and greater than Jonah, for he gives to men his presence and resurrection from the dead, but he does not change God, nor does he spread another Father, but the same one, who always has more for his domestics, and as their love for God progresses, he gives more and greater gifts, just as the Lord said to his disciples: For you will see greater things than these, and Paul says: Not that I have already received or that I have already been justified, but in part we know and in part we prophesy, but when the perfect comes, the things that are in part will be destroyed. Therefore, when the perfect comes, we will not see another Father, but this one whom we now desire to see, for blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God, and we will not expect another Christ and Son of God, but this one who was born of the Virgin Mary, who suffered, in whom we believe and whom we love, just as Isaiah says: They will say in that day: Behold, our Lord God, in whom we have hoped and rejoiced in our salvation, and Peter says in his epistle: Whom you do not see, you love, in whom you now do not see, you have believed, you will rejoice with inexpressible joy, and we will not perceive another Holy Spirit, except this one who is with us and who cries out, Abba, Father, and in the same things, we will have increase and progress, so that we may now enjoy the gifts of God not through a mirror and enigmas, but face to face, thus also now, perceiving more than Solomon, which is the advent of the Son of God, we have not learned another God, except the Creator and Maker of all things, who has been shown to us from the beginning, nor another Christ, Son of God, except the one who was predicted by the prophets. For with the New Testament known and predicted by the prophets, and he who was to dispose it according to the will of the Father was predicted, he was manifested to men as God willed, so that believers in him may always progress, and through the testaments, one salvation and one God, and the precepts that form man are many, and not a few are those that lead man to God. To an earthly and temporal king, indeed, when he is a man, it is permitted to attribute greater progress to those who are subject to him, but to God, it is not permitted, since he is the same, and always wants to bestow greater grace on the human race, and to honor with more gifts those who please him, this is to progress, to find another Father besides the one who was announced from the beginning, and again, besides the one who is thought to have been found a second time, to find another, a third, and of the same progress, from the third to the fourth, and from this again, another and another, and thus, always thinking to progress, such a sense will never stand in God, for it is expelled from the one who is, and turned back, it seeks, indeed, but never finds God, but it will always swim in the depth of incomprehensibility, unless, converted through repentance, it returns from where it was cast out, confessing and believing in one God, the Father, the Creator, who was announced by the Law and the prophets, who was testified by Christ, just as he himself says to those who accused his disciples, as if they did not keep the tradition of the elders: Why do you frustrate the commandment of the Lord because of your tradition? For God said: Honor your father and mother, and, He who curses father or mother, let him die, and again, he says to them a second time: How you have frustrated the word of God because of your tradition, clearly confessing the Father and God, Christ confesses the one who said in the Law: Honor your father and mother, that it may be well with you, for the Word of God confessed the precept of the Law, the true God, and did not call another God, except his own Father.

Quare vos frustramini preeceptum Domini propter traditionem vestram?

pass_b_english: All things are of one and the same substance — that is, they come from one and the same God — just as the Lord says to the disciples: "Therefore every scribe who has been trained for the kingdom of heaven is like a householder who brings out of his treasure what is new and what is old" (Matt 13:52). He did not teach that one person brings out the old and another the new; it is one and the same householder. The Lord is that householder, who rules the whole household of God paternally: to the servants and those still undisciplined he gives a law worthy of them, but to the children, justified by faith, he gives fitting precepts, and to the sons he opens his inheritance. He calls his disciples scribes and teachers of the kingdom of heaven, and of them he also says elsewhere to the Jews: "I send you prophets and wise men and scribes... and you will kill some of them and persecute them from town to town" (Matt 23:34). Thus the new and old brought out of the treasure speak, without contradiction, of the two testaments: the old, which was the former legislation, and the new, which is the way of life according to the Gospel. Of this David says: "Sing to the Lord a new song" (Ps 96:1), and Isaiah: "Sing to the Lord a new hymn" (Isa 42:10). "From the ends of the earth his name is praised; his deeds are proclaimed in the islands" (Isa 24:16; 42:12). And Jeremiah says: "Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will make a new covenant... not like the covenant I made with their fathers at Mount Horeb" (Jer 31:31). Both testaments, however, are produced by one and the same householder — the Word of God, our Lord Jesus Christ — who spoke with Abraham and Moses, who restored liberty to us in newness and multiplied it, which comes from him.

For he says: "Something greater than the temple is here" (Matt 12:6), and "greater than Solomon... greater than Jonah" (Matt 12:41-42), for he gives to men his presence and resurrection from the dead. But he does not change God, nor does he proclaim another Father; he proclaims the same One who always has more for his household, and as their love for God progresses, he gives more and greater gifts — just as the Lord told the disciples: "You will see greater things than these" (John 1:50), and Paul says: "Not that I have already obtained this or am already perfect... For we know in part and we prophesy in part, but when the perfect comes, the partial will pass away" (1 Cor 13:9-10). So when the perfect comes, we will not see another Father, but this One whom we now long to see, for "Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God" (Matt 5:8). We will not wait for another Christ and Son of God, but for this One who was born of the Virgin Mary, who suffered, in whom we believe and whom we love — just as Isaiah says: "They will say in that day: 'Behold, this is our God; we have waited for him, that he might save us. This is the Lord; we have waited for him; let us be glad and rejoice in his salvation'" (Isa 25:9). And Peter says in his epistle: "Though you have not seen him, you love him. Though you do not now see him, you believe in him and rejoice with joy that is inexpressible" (1 Pet 1:8). We will not receive another Holy Spirit, except this One who is with us and cries, "Abba, Father" (Rom 8:15; Gal 4:6). And in these very things we will have increase and progress, so that we may now enjoy the gifts of God not through a mirror and in riddles, but face to face (1 Cor 13:12). Thus also now, perceiving more than Solomon — which is the advent of the Son of God — we have not learned another God besides the Creator and Maker of all things, who was shown to us from the beginning, nor another Christ, Son of God, except the one who was foretold by the prophets.

For with the New Testament known and foretold by the prophets, the One who was to establish it according to the Father's will was also foretold, and he was manifested to men as God willed, so that believers in him may always progress. And through the testaments there is one salvation and one God. The precepts that form a human being are many, and not few are those who lead a human being to God. To an earthly and temporal king, since he is a man, it is permitted to grant greater advancement to those subject to him; but to God, since he is the same and always wills to bestow greater grace on the human race and to honor with more gifts those who please him — is this not progress? To find another Father besides the One announced from the beginning, and then, besides the one thought to have been found a second time, to find a third — and the same progress from a third to a fourth, and from that another and another — so that, always thinking to progress, such a mind will never stand in God. For it is expelled from the One who is, and turning back it seeks but never finds God; it will always swim in the depth of incomprehensibility, unless, converted through repentance, it returns from where it was cast out, confessing and believing in one God, the Father, the Creator, who was announced by the Law and the prophets, who was testified to by Christ — just as he himself says to those who accused his disciples of not keeping the tradition of the elders: "Why do you break the commandment of God for the sake of your tradition? For God commanded, 'Honor your father and your mother,' and, 'Whoever reviles father or mother must surely die.' ... So for the sake of your tradition you have made void the word of God" (Matt 15:3-6). Clearly confessing the Father and God, Christ acknowledges the One who said in the Law: "Honor your father and your mother, that it may go well with you" (Deut 5:16). For the Word of God confessed the precept of the Law; the true God did not call another God except his own Father.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text, including the nuances of the householder metaphor and the theological distinctions regarding the two testaments. All scripture citations in Pass B correctly identify the verses alluded to in the Latin (e.g., Matt 13:52, Ps 96:1, Isa 42:10, Jer 31:31, Matt 15:3-6, etc.). Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source and each other.
